verdict.rationale: Martin's docs describe multiple genuinely autonomous background automations—daily/weekly briefings, proactive email drafting, automatic email triage/labeling, scheduled wake-up calls, and cc-to-schedule meeting booking—plus user-defined multi-step 'shortcuts', all of which run without the user actively prompting each time. Community evidence corroborates ongoing background usage (e.g. todo management alongside coding) and even references the vendor improving 'failure rate' for autonomous actions, though also flags trust/reliability concerns rather than concrete failures. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of the background automations actually firing reliably in practice, and detail on how flexible/custom the automation triggers can be beyond the preset background-task types.
